observations: The cover bows during insertion while the leaves are deflected.
The hooks do not pass fully into engagement beneath the receiver ledges. The leaves remain angled and transmit the insertion bow to the bezel.
Only a tiny outward movement and a click occur; the hook does not move across the ledge.
The rough, low-hanging surface left after support removal requires more sliding force than the leaves provide.
The pump cartridge can slide past comparable roughness under hand force; its weight makes the extra sliding resistance relatively small.
physical_fit: Hooks do not fully engage; insertion deflection remains.
cause_attribution: Derek identifies supported-surface interference as the obstruction to spring-back.
requested_trial: Increase hook reach by approximately 0.5 to 1 mm and restore outward leaf travel.
comparison: Both reach trials use 0.9 mm skirt inset; Mark2 has 0.5 mm extra reach and H2C has 1.0 mm extra reach.
